extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners and patent applicants (practitioners before the Korean Intellectual Property Office)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment and decision rules for amendments to patent specifications and claims under the Korean Patent Act (particularly Article 47 amendments and refusals under Articles 51 and 63), including what constitutes introduction of new matter and which claim amendments are permissible in reply to rejections or reexamination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters described in the specification or drawing(s) as originally filed, and matters that a person skilled in the art would clearly recognize from that disclosure, are deemed included in the scope of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of added matter is measured against the original specification/drawings and what a skilled person would clearly recognize as included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources excluded from assessment of added matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A first country application or a prior-filed application forming the basis of a priority claim shall not be used as the basis of assessment in addition of new matter; an abstract shall not be included in the specification or drawing(s) which forms the basis of assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat priority applications or abstracts as part of the original disclosure when assessing new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of an incomplete invention
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of completing an incomplete invention, the amendment shall be deemed to add new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that complete previously incomplete inventions are generally treated as introducing new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing claim from genus to species
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment narrows a claim from a genus to a species, it introduces new matter unless the species is supported by the original specification/drawings or one skilled in the art would readily recognize the species from the genus at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: changing 'transparent plastic plate' to 'transparent ABS plastic plate' introduces new matter unless ABS is disclosed or obvious to the skilled person. Example2: changing 'sensor detecting rotation' to 'proximity sensor' is allowable if a skilled person would intuitively associate the sensor with a proximity sensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening claim from species to genus
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadening a claim from a species to a genus constitutes introduction of new matter if the genus encompasses other species than the species disclosed in the original specification and those other species may have different functions/effects in addressing the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, deleting limitations described as essential for solving a problem is introduction of new matter; deleting arbitrarily added limitations unrelated to solving the problem may be allowable. Examples: connector shape amendment and traffic-control method example showing when deletion is allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical range amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment adding, changing, or narrowing a numerical range shall be viewed as introduction of new matter unless the new numerical range is disclosed in the original specification or can be derived from the original description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: narrowing melting point ranges may be permissible if derivable from other disclosed temperatures and common laws of nature; otherwise it is new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative limitations (deleting elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment to delete elements from the claims ('negative limitations') is permitted provided the deletion does not introduce any new technical matter not disclosed in the original specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: excluding humans from 'treatment methods for mammals' is permissible where the original disclosure indicates not directed only to particular animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining separate embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining separate configurations or embodiments independently described in the original specification is viewed as introduction of new matter unless the combination is described in the original specification or a skilled person can easily derive the combination considering common technical knowledge at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: combining a 'shaking lever' and a 'conveying unit' into a single refrigerator invention is new matter where the original spec does not describe them attached together or their interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding embodiment or test example
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment to add an embodiment or a test example shall be generally viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: where the added embodiment/test example falls within the scope of the disclosure of the original specification, it may not be new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding new effects of the claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment to add new effects of the claimed invention shall generally be viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: where a skilled person could easily recognize the effects from the disclosed configuration, or where such effects are commonly known for that configuration, they may be allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding titles or short summaries of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment to simply add the title of prior art documents, or both the short summaries and titles, shall not be viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, adding the disclosure of a prior art document to address written-description deficiencies or to compare advantages is generally viewed as introduction of new matter. Example provided regarding adding practice instructions referring to another patent publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding well-known prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the added matter is well-known prior art, if a skilled person does not clearly recognize the added matters as implicitly described in the original specification/drawings, the amendment of adding such well-known prior art shall be deemed addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume well-known status permits adding information unless clearly implicit in the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of obvious errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a skilled person would not only recognize the existence of an error in the specification but also recognize the appropriate correction, an amendment to correct an obvious error does not constitute introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies where one skilled in the art clearly understands which of two or more conflicting descriptions is correct based on the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply to rejections / reexamination must satisfy Article 47(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in reply to the rejection necessitated by a previous amendment or carried out upon a request for reexamination shall additionally satisfy Article 47(3), along with Article 47(2) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition of introduction of new matter under Article 47(2) still applies; the special constraints of 47(3) limit what amendments are acceptable in these contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible categories of claim amendments under Article 47(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to claims in response to a rejection necessitated by a previous amendment or upon a request for reexamination shall be one of: narrowing of claims by restricting claims, correction of clerical errors, clarification of ambiguous descriptions, or deletion of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 47(3) requirements apply only to the amended claims; if an independent claim is amended, dependent claims referring to it are deemed amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine correspondence to Article 47(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an amendment corresponds to allowable cases shall be determined by comparing the claim under examination (upon notice of final rejection) with the claim having the same claim number; if a claim after amendment is clearly the same as the amended claim with a different number, assess by comparison with the claim of the different number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a one-word amendment may be legitimate if it falls under the subparagraphs of Article 47(3); when one claim contains multiple inventions they are assessed individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness note on partial vs whole-claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining whether an amendment meets requirements based on the amended term or phrase may raise fairness issues between an amendment of a whole claim (re-describing the invention) and an amendment to parts of the claim; Article 47(3) is not intended to substantially restrict amendment contents but to prevent examination difficulties caused by excessive amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should be mindful of fairness and the statutory intent when applying Article 47(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of narrowing under Article 47(3)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricting a claim includes internal restriction of the scope recited in the original claim, such as reduction of numerical range, change from genus to species, deletion of alternatively recited elements, and reduction of a referred claim from claims referring to multiple claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction of numerical range means reducing within the original claim's range (simultaneous reduction and extension does not count as reduction). Deleting 'A or B' to remove one alternative is legitimate restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of a claim recognized as legitimate amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Deletion of a claim shall be recognized as a legitimate amendment since it constitutes restriction of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments changing citation numbers or adding cited contents in consequence are deemed corrections of incorrect description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing by adding technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of an invention is narrowed by adding new technical features described in the description or claims (e.g., changing 'B attached to A' to 'B attached to A and then C attached to B').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding features that are supported by the original description is a legitimate narrowing amendment under 47(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases not falling under Article 47(3)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment that newly adds a claim or adds an invention to claims by adding alternative elements or adding a referred claim does not fall under Article 47(3)(i). Inevitable additions resulting from reorganization of claims are exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given where reorganization of claim numbering leads to an unavoidable new claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of amendments that go beyond the original scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include: change from species to genus; deletion of elements from a set; addition and deletion of elements in a set (changing elements present); broadening of numerical range; replacement of element (bolt to rivet); change of numerical range to a non-overlapping range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicitly listed as amendments that take claims beyond original scope and thereby are not allowable as mere 'restriction' under Article 47(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical errors definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Correcting clerical errors refers to cases where descriptions before and after amendment are objectively deemed to be the same (e.g., incorrect claim descriptions explicit from description or obvious by empirical rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such corrections are allowable under Article 47(3)(ii) provided the error is objectively recognizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of ambiguous description
rubrics_metrics.description: An ambiguous description is one whose meaning in context is not clear; includes unclear claim language, mismatch between a claim element and other descriptions, or claims technically unspecified and ambiguous despite clear claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redrafting the overall claim without substantial changes is deemed clarification under Article 47(3)(iii), unless other specific conditions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment deleting new matter (reinstatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new matters were added in an earlier amendment, an amendment reinstating the original claim before the addition of new matter shall be permitted; also permitted are amendments that delete new matter while amending claims according to Article 47(3)(i)-(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimacy is assessed by comparing claims before addition of new matter with the amended claims; examples illustrate when reinstatement or deletion leads to permission or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendments (Article 51) — grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall refuse to enter an amendment if it violates Article 47(2) or (3), or if another ground of rejection is necessitated by the amendment (excluding deletions of a claim among certain amendments), except where exceptions apply (e.g., ex-officio amendment under Article 66(2), ex-officio re-examination under Article 66(3), or request for re-examination under Article 67(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to refuse must be in writing stating the grounds, and generally no appeal is permitted against such a refusal except as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of grounds for rejection (Article 63) and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner intends to reject the application under Article 62 or related conditions, the examiner shall notify the applicant of the ground for rejection and give an opportunity to submit written arguments within a specified period; this does not apply where the examiner intends to refuse to enter an amendment under Article 51(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 63 governs when applicants must be given a chance to respond to proposed rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'new rejection necessitated by the amendment'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'New rejection necessitated by the amendment' means a ground for rejection which did not exist prior to the amendment but newly arises due to the amendment (e.g., claim rendered indefinite or new lack of novelty/inventive step).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection grounds present before the amendment but not notified are not considered 'new' for these purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions when assessing whether to refuse to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex-officio amendment/ex-officio re-examination/amendment upon request, if the previous amendment that should be refused was overlooked, that previous amendment shall be exempt from assessment for refusal; also deletion of a claim is exempt when assessing whether a new rejection is necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exemptions protect against overlooking prior problematic amendments in certain procedural contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination sequencing and multiplicity of unsatisfied requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an amendment meets substantive requirements shall be assessed regardless of order of amendment requirements; if multiple requirements are not satisfied, the examiner should point out as many unsatisfied requirements as possible and refuse to enter the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A flow and sequence are provided for substantive assessment; if amendment is refused, re-examination of the pre-amendment specification is required before final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions when making a decision to refuse to enter amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment contains multiple amended matters, all amended matters must be assessed individually; if any amended matter violates Article 47(2) or (3) or results in a new rejection (except deletion of claim), the whole amendment shall be refused to be entered. The unit of refusal is determined by submitted forms identifying subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple amendments are filed during the response period, refusal is determined per amendment; for applications filed on/after July 1, 2013, earlier amendments are deemed withdrawn and assessment is based on the last-filed amendment. Also: when decisions have been revoked on appeal and remanded, the examiner is bound by the appeal's findings.
